identity.name: Indian rebels of 1857
alt_names: Rebel government of Bahadur Shah Zafar

land.text: Delhi, where the Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was declared 'the Emperor of Hindustan'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Mughal Empire row for 1857-58 is a single 578 km2 cell shape around Delhi.

land.text: the places the rebels took from the Company in 1857

predecessors.note: The Company's land (the east-india-company and british-empire dossiers).

land.text: the last rebel-held places, retaken by 20 June 1858

successors.note: The Company retakes all the rebel-held land; on 1 November 1858 the Crown takes over (british-raj).

capitals.name: Delhi
capitals.note: Bahadur Shah Zafar's seat, May-September 1857; the page names no other rebel capital.

correction.text: Delhi (May-September), Kanpur (June to mid-July) and Awadh, the places the page names as held by the rebels in 1857 (Awadh: the siege and evacuation of Lucknow)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks. Cliopatria's British Empire shape instead cuts 2,210 cells (Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttarakhand) out of 1857-58 and gives them to nobody; the rebels held places and the countryside around them, not that whole area. Awadh as a whole is a reading of the page, which does not map the rebel-held ground.

correction.text: Awadh until 21 March 1858, Jhansi and Bundelkhand until the Central India Field Force, Gwalior from 1 June to about 20 June 1858

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The rebels' ground shrinks through 1858 to Gwalior on 20 June; the ledger's loss events say when each place returns to the Company. Bundelkhand is the page's 'central India (including Bundelkhand and eastern Rajputana)'.

region.text: Delhi, reached by the Meerut mutineers on 11 May 1857, where Bahadur Shah Zafar was declared 'the Emperor of Hindustan'

ledger.note: 10-11 May 1857: the sepoys of the Company's Meerut garrison mutiny on 10 May and reach Delhi the next day; Bahadur Shah Zafar is declared 'the Emperor of Hindustan' (the page dates the proclamation to mid-1857 and says he was coerced by the sepoys and his courtiers to sign it). Delhi is the one Cliopatria cell of the Mughal row in 1857-58.

region.text: the North-Western Provinces, Awadh and central India (Bundelkhand and eastern Rajputana), with parts of Bihar

ledger.note: 10 May 1857: the revolt begins; it was concentrated in the North-Western Provinces, Awadh, central India and parts of Bihar, while Bengal, Bombay and Madras stayed largely calm. The same zone is the british-empire dossier's contest.
11 May 1857: the rebels take Delhi: 'the rebels quickly reached Delhi' in the days after Meerut.
June 1857: the Kanpur sepoys rebel under Nana Sahib and besiege the British entrenchment.
Mid-July 1857: Kanpur 'was retaken by mid-July 1857' with reinforcements.
September 1857: Delhi is retaken 'by the end of September', the siege (about 1 July-21 September) ending on 21 September.

region.text: Lucknow outside the Residency enclave, after the defended enclave was evacuated

ledger.note: 18 November 1857: Campbell's force evacuates the defended enclave at Lucknow, leaving the city to the rebels. The page does not date the rebel takeover of Lucknow; Havelock's relief column reached the city on 25 September without breaking the siege. The reading of the evacuation as the start of rebel control is mine.
21 March 1858: Campbell's second advance ends with the final fighting that drives the rebels out of Lucknow.

March 1858: Hugh Rose's Central India Field Force besieges and captures Jhansi and the Rani flees; the page gives the siege in March and no capture day. The page does not say when the Rani's rising took Jhansi.
1 June 1858: after leaving Jhansi and Kalpi the Rani and the rebel forces capture Gwalior.
17-20 June 1858: the Rani dies in the battle of Gwalior on 17 June and the Company forces recapture the city within three days.
20 June 1858: the rebellion is contained with the rebels' defeat at Gwalior.

region.text: the last rebel-held places, Gwalior, Jhansi and Lucknow

ledger.note: 20 June 1858: the rebel state ends at Gwalior. The page says hostilities were not formally declared ended until 8 July 1859 and that Queen Victoria's proclamation of 1 November 1858 offered amnesty to rebels not involved in murder.

wars.name: Indian Rebellion of 1857

zones.text: the North-Western Provinces, Awadh and central India

wars.outcome: British victory (10 May 1857-20 June 1858); Delhi retaken in September 1857, Lucknow on 21 March 1858, Jhansi in March and Gwalior in June 1858; the Company dissolved under the Government of India Act of 1858.
wars.note: Hostilities not formally ended until 8 July 1859. Hyderabad, Mysore, Travancore, Kashmir and the smaller Rajputana states stayed loyal.

wars.name: Siege of Delhi (1857)
wars.outcome: Delhi retaken by the end of September 1857 after a siege of about 1 July-21 September.

wars.name: Central India campaign (Jhansi and Gwalior)
wars.outcome: Hugh Rose's Central India Field Force takes Jhansi in March 1858; the rebels take Gwalior on 1 June and lose it again by 20 June 1858.

certainty.note: The rebels held cities and the districts around them in a shifting patchwork; the page maps no frontier.

sources.title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
sources.note: The only page used: 10 May 1857-20 June 1858 timeline, Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, Gwalior, the regions of the revolt. It does not mention Birjis Qadr or the Awadh court by name.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-c. A rebel state that Cliopatria lacks and the brief allowed (rule 5): the rebels of 1857 held Delhi for about four months and Awadh and central India into 1858, 13 months in all. One page opened (Indian Rebellion of 1857), so the dossier is thin: the page does not name the Awadh court (Birjis Qadr), does not date the rebel takeover of Lucknow, Jhansi or Kanpur, and maps no rebel frontier. A gap-filler should open 'Siege of Delhi', 'Siege of Lucknow', 'Siege of Cawnpore' and 'Rani of Jhansi' for months and districts, and 'Birjis Qadr' / 'Begum Hazrat Mahal' if the Awadh government is to be a separate colour.
The rebels were several leaderships (Bahadur Shah Zafar at Delhi, Nana Sahib at Kanpur, the Rani of Jhansi, Bakht Khan, Begum Hazrat Mahal, Kunwar Singh) not one government; one dossier is a drawing convenience.
The sibling east-india-company dossier uses the counterpart string 'Indian rebels of 1857 (Bahadur Shah Zafar's Delhi, the Awadh court, Nana Sahib, the Rani of Jhansi)' for the same contest; the slug of this dossier is indian-rebels-of-1857 and british-empire's ledger uses it. Cliopatria's British Empire shape cuts 2,210 cells out for 1857-58; the keyframes here replace the cut with the places the page names.
